newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen futures end slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen futures end slightly higher.

text.p: The key June three-month Euroyen deposit rate futures contract on TIFFE ended Tuesday's day session slightly higher, in line with a volatile Japanese government bond (JGB) futures market, traders said.
The June contract closed up 0.01 at 99.24, after moving between 99.25 and 99.21.
"Euroyen futures were just following JGB futures' moves," a trader at a Japanese brokerage house said.
The June fell from its intraday high after JGB futures gave up much of their gains, traders said.
The key December JGB futures contract closed up 0.15 at 125.47, well off the day's high of 126.12.
"Although the upside for the June Euroyen futures is seen limited, players were forced to cover their short positions as JGB futures showed no signs of weakness," the trader said.
Market participants were also cautious ahead of Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Yasuo Matsushita's regular news conference on Wednesday, traders said.
Traders expect the June contract to remain in a narrow range until the release of the BOJ's key "tankan" corporate survey on November 27.
Interest rate swap (IRS) rates were flat to slightly lower.
At one point in the afternoon, IRS rates that are four-years or longer fell about seven basis points, but bounced back up after JGB futures gave up their gains.
"IRS rates tracked JGB futures' moves," said a trust bank trader.
The five-year IRS rate was quoted at 1.92/1.96 percent, down from 1.94/1.98 percent on Monday.
In the interbank call market, the key unsecured overnight call money was traded at 0.47 percent, unchanged from Monday.
The Bank of Japan (BOJ) injected a net 400 billion yen into the money market this morning, maintaining a neutral stance.
About 10 billion yen worth of three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) was issued at 0.51 percent, unchanged from Friday last week when transactions last took place.
About 40 billion yen worth of one-month CDs was issued at 0.49 percent, unchanged from Monday.
